div.head: IV Eg 2
div.ab: ✠ Woruldgerihta ic wille þæt standen on ælcum leodscipe swa gode swa hy mon betste aredian mæge, Gode to gecwemnysse ⁊ me to fullum cynescipe ⁊ earmum ⁊ eadegum to ðearfe ⁊ to friðe.
Woruldgerihta ic wille þæt standen on ælcum leodscype swa gode swa hi mon betste aredian mæge, Gode to gecwemnysse ⁊ me to fullum cynescype ⁊ earmum ⁊ eadegum to ðearfe ⁊ to friðe.

In nomine sancte et indiuidue Trinitatis moderantis uniuersum orbem præcipio statuere in unaquaque regione terrarum mundane iustitię legem, quantocumque quis inuestigando ordinare ualuerit meliorem, ad immense maiestatis gloriam et honorem diuitibusque ad gaudium et pacem et pauperibus ad plenam consolationem.
Woruldgerihta ic wille þæt standen on ælcum leodscype swa gode swa hi mon betste aredian mæge, Gode to gecwemnysse ⁊ me to fullum cynescype ⁊ earmum ⁊ eadegum to ðearfe ⁊ to friðe.

✠ Weltliche Rechte will ich, dass in jeder Völkerschaft so gute bestehen, wie man sie als beste ausfindig machen kann, Gott zum Wohlgefallen und mir zur vollen Königswürde und Armen und Reichen zum Nutzen und zur Sicherheit.
✠ I will that secular rights stand in every nation as good as they can best be devised, to the pleasure of God and to my full royal dignity, and to the benefit and security of poor and rich.

My will is that the rights of the laity be maintained in every province at the best standard which can be devised, in accordance with what will be acceptable to God, and will preserve my royal dignity unimpaired, and tend to the advantage and security of rich and poor.

✠It is my will that secular rights be in force in every province, as good as they can best be devised, to the satisfaction of God, and for my full royal dignity and for the benefit and security of poor and rich;

Cf. above Pro².—The Versio borrows its solemn opening from charter style: In nomine s. Trinitatis a. 969 Bi 1231; Christi . . . rerum moderantis habenas 1258

Nicht allein ‘Gesetze’, sondern ‘Verfassungszustände’, einschliesslich (wie folgender Satz lehrt) subjektiver Anrechte des Königs und Adels, insofern sie nicht schon allein dem Eigentum entfliessen, daher nebengeordnet den bisher behandelten Kirchenprivilegien

Not only ‘laws’ but ‘constitutional conditions’, including (as the following sentence shows) subjective rights of the king and the nobility, in so far as these do not flow from ownership alone; hence placed alongside the church privileges dealt with so far

Nicht ‘allem Volke’. Es sind mehr als zwei gemeint (sonst stände ‘beide’), und zwar—wie auch Toller s. v. leodscipe versteht—laut 2, 2 Engländer, Nordleute (s. Gl Denalagu 4—b. 9. a), Brythonen; s. Gl Briten 2. a. Eadred schon hatte sich 949 genannt rex Anglorum rectorque Norðanhymbra et paganorum imperator Brittonumque propugnator; Birch 882. 884. Vgl. Gl Königstitel 4b, wo hinter Merciorum ausgefallen ist: et Norðanhymbrorum

Not ‘all the people’. More than two peoples are meant (otherwise ‘both’ would be used), namely—as Toller s. v. leodscipe also understands it—according to 2, 2, the English, the Northmen (see Gl Denalagu 4—b. 9. a) and the Brythons; see Gl Briten 2. a. Eadred had already in 949 styled himself rex Anglorum rectorque Norðanhymbra et paganorum imperator Brittonumque propugnator; Birch 882. 884. Cf. Gl Königstitel 4b, where after Merciorum the words et Norðanhymbrorum have dropped out
‘to find out what is appropriate’ Toller Suppl. s. v., sinngemässer als früheres ‘to execute’. Schon das Beschliessen der Gesetze gereicht zur Königswürde laut II Eg Pro
‘to find out what is appropriate’ Toller Suppl. s. v., closer to the sense than the earlier ‘to execute’. According to II Eg Pro, the mere enacting of laws redounds to the royal dignity

The Versio again puffs itself up in more bombastic style
